items.item_text: Oversee daily facilities operations, assign work, monitor project progress, and ensure appropriate staffing and scheduling.

Provide service to the campus community, prioritizing the needs of students and the academic mission while ensuring timely and effective support for the President’s Office, institutional events, and campus activities.
Insure regular building inspections are completed, assess facility conditions, and recommend maintenance, repairs, and improvements.
Manage equipment, supplies, inventory, and procurement to support efficient departmental operations.
Coordinate facilities services with campus departments to minimize disruptions and support events, activities, and summer programs.
Support the Associate Director of Maintenance and Construction, where needed, regarding maintenance, renovations, and construction projects.
Work alongside the Assistant Director of Planning, Capital Projects and Construction on contractor and vendor relationships, ensuring compliance with service agreements and performance standards.
Supervise staff performance, conduct evaluations, and address employee development and performance concerns in collaboration with Human Resources.
Assist with departmental budget development, monitoring, and resource allocation.
Support campus sustainability initiatives, safety compliance, emergency preparedness, and response efforts.
Provide leadership and operational support to the AVP, represent Facilities on institutional matters, and respond to after-hours operational needs as required.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Strong leadership and supervisory skills, with the ability to foster a positive, collaborative work environment, build morale, and promote accountability among a diverse workforce.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; Spanish language proficiency highly desirable.
Knowledge of custodial operations, including cleaning methods, materials, chemicals, equipment, and workplace safety standards.
Ability to independently prioritize responsibilities, exercise sound judgment, and effectively manage multiple operational demands with minimal supervision.
Experience training, coaching, and developing employees, including conducting performance evaluations and addressing performance concerns.
Ability to manage budgets, payroll, and timekeeping records.
Stand for prolonged periods of time;
Operate a computer;
Communicated with others by email, in person and over the phone;
Read printed materials and a computer screen;
Have the mobility to use standard office equipment;
Stand, walk, bend, climb, push, pull, stoop, twist, stretch;
Lift up to 50 pounds from ground to waist level without assistance;
climb ladders up to 20 feet with assistance and up to ten feet unassisted; and j
Have the stamina tow manage a high-volume workload in fast-paced environment and occasional long hours.
Cover Letter: Indicate your reason for interest in this position, describe how your qualifications make youan ideal candidate, and explain which of Pitzer’s core values best relates to your own.
Resume: List relevant qualifications and dates of experience.

Professional References: References will be contacted for select applicants and advance notice will be provided. Provide the names of at least three (3) individuals who can speak to your professional qualifications. Include their business titles, contact information and an indication of how you are acquainted with them (e.g., former supervisor, coworker, etc.).
Campus Security Authority Reporter (CSA ): Employees responsible for reporting crimes that are disclosed to them, so that crime statistics reporting is as accurate as possible.

Federal Educational Rights and Privacy Act Reporter (FERPA) : Employees with access to student records and information must adhere to the privacy protection requirements under FERPA, which restricts what student information may be disclosed and to whom.
Mandatory Reporter : Employees who have frequent contact with children are required to report all known or suspected cases of child abuse or neglect.

Responsible Employee : Any employee who has the authority to take action to redress sexual violence, who has been given the duty of reporting incidents of sexual violence or any other misconduct by students to the Title IX Coordinator or other appropriate School designee; or whom a student could reasonably believe has this authority or duty.
